title: BMD REST camera payload profile
description: Validates payloads/models/<MODEL_KEY>/rest/<FIRMWARE>.json files at load time (camera_profile.validate_rest_profile). Populated from tools/rest/probe_endpoints.py sweep output (build_rest_profile_block's exact shape) — never hand-authored. See docs/rest/transport.md and CLAUDE.md design principle 6's REST sibling rule: no endpoint is trusted until swept on that exact camera, firmware, and transport.

status.description: Whole-profile status, mirroring the BLE schema's _meta.status. UNVERIFIED until a write probe has confirmed a *changing* value on a real camera, not just a same-value PUT.

transport.description: Which transport this sweep ran over. A result on one is not evidence about the other — see docs/rest/transport.md.

endpoints.description: REST path -> sweep outcome, keyed exactly as tools/rest/probe_endpoints.py reports it (e.g. "/system/format", "/audio/channel/0/level").

websocket_properties.description: Property paths that successfully subscribed over the WebSocket event feed during the sweep.

format_names.description: Confirmed REST codec strings per family/variant, e.g. {"BRAW": {"5:1": "BRaw:5_1"}, "ProRes": {"422": "Original"}}. Not derived from a naming rule in code (design principle 1) — REST's spelling can diverge from the BLE profile's (BRaw's ':' -> '_' is a rule; ProRes's '422' -> 'Original' is not, confirmed on POCKET_6K_G2 v8.6, docs/rest/transport.md).

additionalProperties.description: Codec family -> {variant name -> REST codec string}.

endpointResult.description: One endpoint's sweep outcome. status/supported come from the read sweep; put_status/put_supported are only present when --probe-writes ran for this path.

status.description: HTTP status from the read sweep's GET. null means the request never got a reply (cable unplugged, wrong host, firewall) — see ProbeResult.status.

supported.description: Whether a caller should use this endpoint for reads — true only for a 2xx GET. A 501 (camera correctly declining) and a 5xx (firmware defect) are both false, deliberately not distinguished by this flag alone; see `status` for that.

notes.description: The exception message when status is null, or another free-text note.

put_status.description: HTTP status from the idempotent same-value PUT probe.

put_supported.description: Whether PUT is implemented on this endpoint. A same-value PUT proves the endpoint exists, not that a changing write applies — see docs/rest/transport.md.

provenance.description: Same shape as the BLE schema's provenance $def, deliberately kept structurally identical so REST endpoints carry VERIFIED/CANDIDATE/UNVERIFIED per firmware just as BLE commands do.

status.description: CANDIDATE = swept and either not yet re-run or only same-value-probed. VERIFIED = a changing write has been confirmed on real hardware for the endpoints this profile guards.
